review_notes: I read the whole supplied file from the text given. I did not open Mathlib or the related Tau Ceti files, so this verdict rests on the file's own content. The file adds three private definitions, `Settled`, `arms` and `unsettledPrefix`, plus the lemmas and main theorem that use them. Each definition is specific to this uncrossing argument. `Settled` says no crossing pair remains to the right of and below a corner. `arms` is a filtered finset of positive cells in a corner's row and column. `unsettledPrefix` is a filtered finset of lexicographic prefixes that contain an unsettled corner. None of these matches an existing Mathlib concept on the same assumptions. The ordering uses Mathlib's `ι ×ₗ κ` lexicographic product, and the induction uses `Relation.ReflTransGen`, `Finset.card_lt_card` and `Nat.strong_induction_on`, so the file already reuses existing notions. The measure-and-induct argument is a proof technique, not a competing definition. I found no competing concept, so I report nothing. The only remaining uncertainty is that I did not search Mathlib for a closer match to `unsettledPrefix`. I would not expect one to justify a finding, because the definition is private and only serves the termination measure.
